description: Lists grouped field rules (MANDATORY, WARNING, FORMULA) by rule_group_id. Omit rule_type to return all three. Optionally filter by repeated rule_type, asset_type_id, and trigger_field. A rule without a group id is returned as a singleton group.

parameters.name: rule_type
parameters.description: Optional repeatable rule-type filter (MANDATORY, WARNING, FORMULA). Omit to return all grouped types.

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Locale for localized response messages (for example: en, fr-FR, pseudo)

items.description: Grouped conditional-validation rule (aggregates granular rows sharing a rule_group_id)

id.description: Representative granular rule id (the first row in the group)

project_id.description: Project this group applies to; null for company-level rules

rule_group_id.description: Group id linking the granular rules; null for an ungrouped singleton

rule_type.description: Rule type shared by every rule in the group

asset_type_ids.description: Asset type ids in the group; a single null entry means 'all asset types'

trigger_field_ids.description: Trigger field ids in the group

conditions.description: Conditions AST for a conditional-validation rule

definition.description: Structured rule definition. Shape depends on rule_type: FieldRuleDefinitionDTO for NAMING, FieldDefaultsDefinitionDTO for FIELD_DEFAULTS, ConditionalValidationDefinitionDTO for MANDATORY/WARNING, F...

is_active.description: Whether the group's rules are active

granular_rule_count.description: Number of granular rules in the group

validation_errors.description: Optional read-time health findings for this grouped rule.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax or parameters that fail to meet validation requirements.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.
